summary: As part of a hackathon, a Python algorithm was developed for the sonification of video sequences depicting a CO₂ emissions model. The algorithm performs a frame-by-frame analysis of image color characteristics, matches pixels against five target color references, and maps the proportion of each color onto the amplitude of a corresponding voice. As a result, a five-voice musical sequence is generated that captures the temporal dynamics of the emissions. The resulting videos with musical accompaniment are published on a web platform built with React. Users can simultaneously observe the visualization and perceive its auditory representation while comparing different scenarios. The relevance of the project is driven by the need for accessible climate data communication: integrating scientific visualization, parameter-mapping sonification, and web technologies enhances audience engagement and raises awareness of the scale of CO₂ emissions.
details:
The project transforms video recordings of a CO₂ emissions model into music via parameter-mapping sonification, wherein the color semantics of scientific visualization serve directly as musical material: color determines pitch, while its prevalence within a frame governs the volume of the corresponding voice. Technically, the process is implemented through a Python script utilizing the NumPy library, which decodes video frame-by-frame via ffmpeg, downscales frame resolution to optimize computational efficiency, and performs pixel-by-pixel matching of color values against five target color references in the RGB color space. To mitigate the effects of noise and lighting variations, the algorithm filters images by red-channel range, saturation, and hue, discarding white, gray, green, and blue pixels. For each frame, the proportion of pixels matching each target color is calculated and mapped onto the amplitude of an individual voice, whereas the overall proportion of chromatic pixels regulates the master volume. Subsequently, the resulting values are temporally interpolated to ensure inter-frame color stability, smoothed using attack/release envelopes for seamless musical transitions, and synthesized into a stereophonic five-voice melody with spatial voice panning.

All processing is executed locally, yielding both a final video with musical accompaniment and a standalone audio-only file, encoded in MP4 format using ffmpeg. To effectively present the generated materials to the audience, a web platform was developed using React, Tailwind CSS, and React Router. The generated media files are manually added to the repository, after which the build and deployment of the website are automatically executed via Git and GitHub Actions with publication on GitHub Pages. During system development, the team addressed several critical factors: high performance of frame-by-frame analysis, cross-browser audio format compatibility, proper operation of SPA routes on GitHub Pages, and user-friendly on-site track playback.

The developed algorithm is deterministic, reproducible, and adaptable to various emission scenarios, enabling users to audibly perceive temporal dynamics that are difficult to discern in static charts. Combining visual and auditory perception forms a distinct "sonic portrait" of emissions, transforming analytical data into an emotionally comprehensible experience, enhancing audience engagement, and making the information more accessible. The project is expected to contribute to the popularization of climate research and raise awareness of the scale of CO₂ emissions, finding practical application in education, media, and scientific communication for the intuitive comparison of different scenarios.
